title: Cloud Application Risk Profiles in Cloud App Control
aliases: why was this app caught by my risk rule

prose.text: A Risk Profile lets a rule match applications by attribute instead of by name. It is how "block every unsanctioned, high-risk file-sharing app" is written without listing apps. {{where-configured}}

prose.label: How a profile combines its attributes.
Cloud application tags.
prose.text: {{tags-what}} {{tags-limit}} {{tags-page}} Whether predefined tags exist and how a tag is attached to an application are open {{gap:tag-association}}.

A rule that selects a profile applies to every matching app, so one rule can account for many blocks: [[zia.cloud-app-control.rule-criteria]]. {{attribute-sources-3p}} Where the other attribute values come from is open {{gap:attribute-sources}}. The Application Information page itself is in [[portfolio.saas-security-report]].

checks.do: Whether each selected criterion of the rule's profile is satisfied by the app's current attribute values, since the attributes combine with AND.
Whether the match is explained from the rule's profile and the app's attributes, not from the app's name.
Whether a Risk Index override on the app explains a change in matching, since overrides are evaluated when the Risk Index criterion matches.

where-configured.statement: A Cloud Application Risk Profile is created under Data Security > Inline CASB > Risk Profiles (Add Cloud Application Risk Profile) and then associated with Cloud App Control rules; the profile name is what the rule form displays.
where-configured.conditions: Corrected on recapture (2026-10-18): previously "A Cloud Application Risk Profile is created under Administration > Risk Profiles (Cloud Application tab) and then associated with Cloud App Control rules; the profile name is what the rule form displays." The recaptured page gives the Data Security > Inline CASB path.

quotes: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > Inline CASB > Risk Profiles.
Click Add Cloud Application Risk Profile.
creating a cloud application risk profile and associating the profile with the Cloud App Control policy rules.
Profile Name: Enter the name of the cloud application risk profile. This is displayed when configuring the Cloud App Control policy rules.

composition.statement: A profile is a series of AND operators between its attributes (Application Status, Hosting Information, Security Information). The attributes that allow multiple values (Risk Index, Certificates Supported, Data Encryption in Transit, SSL Cert Key Size) are OR between their own values.

quotes: The cloud application risk profile consists of a series of AND operators placed between the attributes in the Application Status, Hosting Information, and Security Information sections

The attributes that allow multiple value selection (Risk Index, Certificates Supported, Data Encryption in Transit, and SSL Cert Key Size) consist of a series of OR operators placed between the values in them

example.statement: Zscaler's example profile is [Risk Index (1 OR 3 OR 5)] AND [Application Status (Sanctioned)] AND [Certificates Supported (AICPA OR GDPR)] AND [SSL Pinned (Yes)].

quotes: For example, [Risk Index (1 (OR) 3 (OR) 5)] (AND) [Application Status (Sanctioned)] (AND) [Certificates Supported (AICPA (OR) GDPR)] (AND) [SSL Pinned (Yes)].

core-attributes.statement: The core attributes are Risk Index (1 to 5, 1 lowest risk), Application Status (Sanctioned or Unsanctioned), Tags, Certificates Supported (include or exclude), Password Strength (Good, Poor, Unknown), Data Encryption in Transit (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3, Unknown) and SSL Cert Key Size (256, 384, 768, 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, 8192 Bits, Unknown).
core-attributes.conditions: Corrected on recapture (2026-10-18): the SSL Cert Key Size list previously read "(Any, 2048, 256, 3072, 384, 4096 Bits, Unknown)". The recaptured page drops Any and adds 768, 1024 and 8192 Bits.

quotes: Risk Index: Select the risk index number (1–5, 1 being the lowest risk and 5 being the highest
Application Status: Select the application status. You can select either Sanctioned or Unsanctioned
Tags: Select the tags associated with the application.
Certificates Supported: Select the supported certifications for the application. You can choose to either include or exclude certificates
Password Strength: Select one of the following options that represent how secure your password is for the application:
Good: Require users to set passwords
Poor: Require users to set passwords
Unknown: Have no restriction on the strength or complexity of the passwords.
Data Encryption in Transit: Select the data encryption versions (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3, or Unknown
SSL Cert Key Size: Select a cert key size (256 Bits, 384 Bits, 768 Bits, 1024 Bits, 2048 Bits, 3072 Bits, 4096 Bits, 8192 Bits, or Unknown).

tags-what.statement: A cloud application tag groups cloud applications (custom, predefined or both, across categories) to the organization's needs. The feature has three parts: creating the tag, associating it with cloud applications, and creating risk profiles with it, so Cloud App Control policies can act on tag-based risk profiles.

quotes: Zscaler's cloud application tag allows you to logically group cloud applications based on your organization's requirements.
Group cloud applications (i.e., custom or predefined applications or both) from different categories based on your organization's requirements.
Creating a cloud application tag.
Associating the tag with the cloud application.
Creating risk profiles with this tag.
Handle traffic to specific cloud applications by applying cloud app control policies with tag-based risk profiles.

tags-limit.statement: An organization can create at most 16 cloud application tags, each up to 127 characters, and a tag is created by entering a Tag Name.

quotes: You can create a maximum of 16 tags.
In the Add Cloud Application Tag drawer, enter a name for the cloud application tag in the Tag Name field.
| Cloud Application Tags per Organization | 16 tags | Each tag can have up to 127 characters. |

risk-index-overrides.statement: Applications with risk index overrides set on the Application Information page are evaluated in the policy when the Risk Index criterion matches.

quotes: All the cloud applications, including those with risk index overrides from the Application Information page, are evaluated in the policy if the risk index criterion matches.

tag-association.title: Whether predefined cloud application tags exist and how a tag is attached to an application
tag-association.blocks: explaining how an application comes to carry a tag
tag-association.detail: The Cloud Application Tags articles describe creating a tag and list associating it with the cloud application as a step, but the association step is on the About Cloud Applications and Application Information pages, which are outside the captured set. The Add drawer shows only a Tag Name; no captured page says whether predefined tags exist.

attribute-sources.title: Who supplies each risk attribute value
attribute-sources.blocks: explaining why an app's attribute value differs from expectation
attribute-sources.detail: Partly answered by attribute-sources-3p: six Application Information fields are stated as populated by Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance; and by tags-what and tags-limit, which show that the Tags attribute is a grouping the organization creates (up to 16). The other attribute values remain unattributed. The captures say the Risk Index is a score assigned from risk attribute values, that Application Status and Tags have their own pages, and that the Risk Index can be overridden per app. They do not say which attribute values Zscaler maintains and which the customer sets. The earlier ledger named Zscaler ThreatLabz as the maintainer; no registered source says so, so that is not carried as a claim.
